models.target: New command pair and contrasting finite number forms in supporting systems.
models.explanation: The command pair distinguishes one addressee from several. Ordinary indicative third-person number contrasts use the selected present or dental-past endings; do not add personal endings to a participle or confuse an indicative with the corresponding command.
models.alternatives: Accept the documented variants within their stated lexical and morphological scope. A valid variant does not justify an unassigned sense or syntax.

models.model: When the monk came, the man gave him water.
models.explanation: Ðā se munuc cōm is the temporal subordinate clause; cōm is third singular preterite indicative. The second ðā resumes it as then in the main clause, whose sealde is third singular preterite indicative. Him is the monk as dative recipient.
models.alternatives: When the monk arrived, then the man gave him water; idiomatic English may omit then.
models.diagnosis: Do not read either ðā as a plural article or make sealde a subjunctive solely because its spelling can be syncretic.
models.target: Factual past when/then; conjunction and correlating adverb.

models.model: When you come, I help you.
models.explanation: The context is repeated visits. Gē cumað is the temporal subordinate clause, with second plural present indicative; the second ðonne is correlating then, and helpe is first singular present indicative in its stated main-clause context. Ēow is a plural dative governed by helpan.
models.alternatives: Whenever you come, I help you; then I help you preserves the explicit correlate.
models.diagnosis: Do not translate temporal ðonne as than or infer a subjunctive from first-singular helpe alone.
models.target: Recurring when/then, without a comparative-than analysis.

models.model: While he ate, I carried water. Both statements express the same simultaneous relation.
models.explanation: Ðā-hwīle-ðe and mid-ðȳ introduce the overlapping circumstance. Ǣt is third singular and bær first singular preterite indicative. Neither conjunction alone asserts that eating caused the carrying.
models.alternatives: As he was eating, I carried water; an English progressive is a contextual translation, not a new Old English tense analysis.
models.diagnosis: Do not make the accompanying action a causal clause merely because it precedes the main clause.
models.target: Simultaneous while expressed by two selected temporal connections.

models.model: Do not go before I come. Be here until I come.
models.explanation: Both come-events are still anticipated. Cume is first singular present subjunctive in the selected clauses; the surface is identical to the first singular indicative, so the stated construction and context identify the analysis. Far and wes are singular imperatives.
models.alternatives: Stay here until I come is idiomatic for the second instruction. Other evidenced temporal choices may be valid language but must satisfy the stated target.
models.diagnosis: Do not force an English will auxiliary or claim that the spelling cume alone distinguishes mood.
models.target: Anticipated before/until and the bounded present subjunctive.

models.model: I help you because you are sick.
models.explanation: For-ðon-ðe ðū eart untrum gives the factual reason; ic helpe ðē is the explained action. Eart is second singular present indicative. Ðē is the dative person helped.
models.alternatives: Since you are sick can render the causal force if since is clearly causal.
models.diagnosis: Do not reverse cause and consequence or label the clause a purpose.
models.target: Factual cause with indicative and accurate clause relations.

models.model: I know that the monk comes. The monk comes so that he may help me. The monk is so good that he helps me.
models.explanation: The first ðæt clause supplies known content and has cymð, third singular present indicative. The second states intended purpose and has helpe, third singular present subjunctive. The last states a result and has hilpð, third singular present indicative. The same spelling ðæt does not fix its function.
models.alternatives: The monk is coming / comes can fit the present setting. Purpose may be rendered in order to help me, provided the finite Old English subject and mood are identified.
models.diagnosis: Do not call the intended act an asserted accomplished result or convert every ðæt clause to subjunctive.
models.target: Same conjunction spelling with three distinct functions and contextually appropriate moods.

models.model: The man held the animal lest it take the food.
models.explanation: The intended prevention concerns the animal's taking the food. Nōme is third singular preterite subjunctive, related to the past holding. The negative-purpose conjunction already expresses prevention; the sentence does not assert that the animal took food.
models.alternatives: So that it would not take the food; to prevent it from taking the food.
models.diagnosis: Do not negate the holding or assert the feared outcome happened.
models.target: Negative purpose, not negation of the main action or assertion of the feared outcome.

models.model: Although he is sick, he helps me.
models.explanation: Sīe is third singular present subjunctive of wesan. The concessive clause admits a circumstance despite which the main event occurs. The stipulated factual illness is compatible with this ordinary concessive subjunctive.
models.alternatives: Though he is sick; even though he is sick.
models.diagnosis: Subjunctive here does not imply that his illness is false or uncertain.
models.target: Concession can concede a fact; subjunctive is not a synonym for false.

models.model: If he is here, he helps me. If he were here, he would help me.
models.explanation: The open condition uses present indicatives is and hilpð. The explicitly contrary-present setting uses preterite subjunctives wǣre and hulpe; these refer to the present hypothetical situation, not to earlier completed events. Gif alone does not impose mood.
models.alternatives: He will help me can suit a forward-looking consequence in the first open setting; the second must preserve the stated absence now.
models.diagnosis: Do not translate the second as a past factual visit, or insert willan mechanically for English would.
models.target: Open indicative condition versus explicitly contrary-present preterite subjunctive condition.

models.model: When does the monk come? When the monk comes, I help him. The monk is older than the fisherman.
models.explanation: Hwonne asks a direct question. Initial ðonne in the second sentence introduces a temporal clause. In the last, ðonne introduces the comparison standard, with the repeated copula understood and fiscere nominative.
models.alternatives: When is the monk coming?; whenever the monk comes, in the stated recurring use.
models.diagnosis: Do not merge the three functions into a single when or than rule.
models.target: When-question, when-clause and than-standard are distinct functions.

models.model: The fisherman came to help the man. The fisherman came so that the monk might help the man.
models.explanation: The earlier cuman plus tō-inflected-infinitive frame has the fisherman's own helping as its purpose. The finite clause explicitly makes se munuc the subject of hulpe. The dative męnn is the person helped in each.
models.alternatives: In order to help; in order that the monk should help.
models.diagnosis: Do not impose the main-clause subject on an explicitly different finite purpose-clause subject.
models.target: Earlier same-subject purposive infinitive contrasted with finite purpose and its own subject.

models.model: It is the day when he came.
models.explanation: Ðe relates the coming to its temporal antecedent se dæg. It does not ask a question and does not set an if condition. Cōm is third singular preterite indicative.
models.alternatives: It is the day on which he came.
models.diagnosis: Do not replace the temporal relative with direct-question hwonne merely because English uses when.
models.target: Bounded temporal relative after day, needed by Cook V.18.7.

models.model: Ðā se fæder cōm, ðā sealde se sunu him wæter.
models.target: Past when/then correlation; father as temporal subject, son as giving subject, father as dative recipient.
models.alternatives: Defensible clause order and an explicit dative father phrase are acceptable; retain the required ðā … ðā target.
models.diagnosis: Subject and recipient must not be reversed.
old_english_outputs: Ðā se fæder cōm, ðā sealde se sunu him wæter.

models.model: Ðonne ðā fisceras cumað, ðonne sęlð se cyning him męte.
models.target: Recurring temporal indicative; plural fishermen and dative plural him.
models.alternatives: A defensible expanded dative noun phrase or word order; retain the requested correlation.
models.diagnosis: Do not use past-event ðā for the requested recurring sense or singular cymð with fisceras.
old_english_outputs: Ðonne ðā fisceras cumað, ðonne sęlð se cyning him męte.

models.model: Mid-ðȳ ðā fisceras sǣton on ðǣm hūse, se sunu bær wæter.
models.target: Factual simultaneous past clauses with selected mid-ðȳ, plural sitting subject and singular carrying subject.
models.alternatives: The main clause may use an evidenced correlating ðā; another conjunction can be valid but would miss the stated mid-ðȳ target.
models.diagnosis: Sǣton and bær express the given past events; do not make one a purpose of the other or use a singular verb with plural fishermen.
old_english_outputs: Mid-ðȳ ðā fisceras sǣton on ðǣm hūse, se sunu bær wæter.

models.model: Ne far, ǣr ic cume.
models.target: One addressee; singular imperative and anticipated-before clause.
models.alternatives: Do not go before I arrive is the intended sense; documented word-order variants accepted.
models.diagnosis: The anticipated event requires the selected subjunctive analysis; cume is syncretic with the first indicative and must be explained contextually.

models.model: Wesað on ðǣm hūse, oð-ðæt ðā fisceras cumen.
models.target: Plural command, ordinary locative dative and plural present subjunctive for the anticipated coming.
models.alternatives: Bēoð is an available alternative command; the selected context is waiting for an unrealized arrival.
models.diagnosis: Cumen, not ordinary indicative cumað, satisfies the requested anticipated-until target; command number must address several people.
old_english_outputs: Wesað on ðǣm hūse, oð-ðæt ðā fisceras cumen.

models.model: Se munuc sęlð ðǣm męnn wæter, for-ðon-ðe se mann is ðurstig.
models.target: Factual cause with indicative and agreeing predicate adjective.
models.essential_meaning: The monk gives the man water; the man’s thirst is the reason.
models.alternatives: A different defensible order or a pronoun with clear reference is acceptable.
models.diagnoses: The recipient is dative; the thirsty man is nominative and controls the adjective. Do not introduce an unaudited thirst verb.
old_english_outputs: Se munuc sęlð ðǣm męnn wæter, for-ðon-ðe se mann is ðurstig.

models.model: Ðā fisceras cōmon, ðæt se munuc him hulpe.
models.target: Plural past main subject, different singular purpose subject, dative plural people helped.
models.alternatives: Defensible order and explicit dative fiscerum; retain a finite purpose clause rather than substitute the earlier same-subject infinitive.
models.diagnosis: The monk, not the fishermen, is the subject of helping; him can be dative plural here.
old_english_outputs: Ðā fisceras cōmon, ðæt se munuc him hulpe.

models.model: Ðā męnn wǣron swā hungrige, ðæt hīe ǣton ðone męte.
models.target: Plural predicate agreement and factual past result with indicative ǣton.
models.alternatives: Defensible word order and a repeated subject in place of hīe; preserve an asserted result.
models.diagnosis: Do not replace indicative ǣton with an unassigned purpose subjunctive or leave the masculine plural adjective singular.
old_english_outputs: Ðā męnn wǣron swā hungrige, ðæt hīe ǣton ðone męte.

models.model: Ðā fisceras hēoldon ðā dēor, ðȳ-lǣs-ðe ðā dēor ūrne męte nōmen.
models.target: Past holding intended to prevent plural animals from taking food; nōmen is plural preterite subjunctive.
models.alternatives: Pronoun hīe for the animals is defensible with a clear antecedent; preserve the purpose of prevention.
models.diagnosis: The source of negative force is the conjunction; do not assert the taking happened or make our agree with the animals rather than singular męte.
old_english_outputs: Ðā fisceras hēoldon ðā dēor, ðȳ-lǣs-ðe ðā dēor ūrne męte nōmen.

models.model: Ðēah se munuc wǣre untrum, hē healp ðǣm męnn.
models.target: Admitted factual illness with concessive preterite subjunctive; past indicative consequence and dative helped person.
models.alternatives: Ðēah ðe if assigned as a documented alternative; grammatical alternatives remain separate from a selected-form target.
models.diagnosis: Wǣre need not deny the illness; do not mistake healp for the similar subjunctive hulpe.
old_english_outputs: Ðēah se munuc wǣre untrum, hē healp ðǣm męnn.

models.model: Gif se cyning wǣre hēr, hē hulpe ūs.
models.target: Both preterite subjunctives refer to the present contrary-to-fact setting; ūs is dative plural.
models.alternatives: Accept defensible clause order; no new willan auxiliary is necessary.
models.diagnosis: Do not change the stipulated time to past or infer that gif always requires this pair.
old_english_outputs: Gif se cyning wǣre hēr, hē hulpe ūs.

models.target: Translate the complete 59-word new account, preserving its purpose, timing, concession, reference and reciprocal help.
models.model: The old fisherman came to the house so that he might help his son. When he came, the son was hungry. He gave him food. While the son ate, the fisherman carried water. Although the fisherman was old, he helped his son. The son said, ‘Be here until I come.’ He went away and came back and gave his father water.
models.translation_origin: Curriculum designer independent translation witness, prepared before viewing source-editor or coordinator private witnesses.

models.model: Purpose: ðæt hē his suna hulpe, explaining why the father came; hulpe is third singular preterite subjunctive. While: Mid-ðȳ se sunu ǣt, giving simultaneous eating; ǣt is third singular preterite indicative. Concession: Ðēah se fiscere wǣre eald, admitting age despite which he helps; wǣre is third singular preterite subjunctive.
models.diagnosis: Do not call all dependent clauses conditions or read preterite subjunctive as necessarily unreal past.
models.target: Three adverbial functions in connected narration.

models.model: The fisherman/father gives food to his son: se fiscere names the subject and him is understood as the son, the dative recipient. At the end the son gives water to his father; hē continues the son after his own direct speech, his refers to the son, and fæder has the selected endingless dative singular. Reference uses the discourse, not morphological gender alone.
models.diagnosis: Case and discourse determine the recipient; the endingless fæder does not force a nominative subject. A pronoun's masculine singular shape alone does not name one of the two men uniquely.
models.target: Track agents, dative recipients and possessors through connected clauses.

models.model: Ic is the son who is speaking. His coming is still expected when he tells his father to be here; cume is first singular present subjunctive in the anticipated-until clause. The later cōm, following the son's departure, fulfills it.
models.diagnosis: The direct quotation's first person is not the narrator or father. Cume is formally syncretic with first singular indicative; identify the selected anticipated-until analysis from context, not spelling alone.
models.target: Direct-speech reference, anticipated-until relation and later narrative fulfillment.
Translate the entire exact observation, retaining the metals, jet description and conditional claim; all helps remain available.
models.model: Likewise it is also rich in veins of metal—copper and iron, lead and silver. Jet is also found here; the stone is a black gem. If one puts it in fire, then snakes flee away from there.
models.translation_origin: Curriculum designer independent translation witness, prepared before viewing source-editor or coordinator private witnesses.

models.model: The condition is gif man hine on fȳr dēð, if one puts it in fire. The main clause is ðonne flēoð ðǣr næddran onwęg, then snakes flee away from there. Dēð is third singular present indicative of dōn; flēoð is third plural present indicative of flēon. Ðonne is the main-clause correlate then, not than.
models.diagnosis: The unfamiliar generic man and flight form are supplied; explaining them does not confer independent recall.
models.target: Indicative general condition and correlating then; supplied unfamiliar forms remain visible.

models.model: First hit refers to Britain/the island in the introduction, a neuter referent. Hine refers to the masculine stone just named and is accusative as the thing put into the fire. The source changes referent; it does not use two interchangeable pronouns for one noun.
models.diagnosis: Do not let nearest English word order erase the supplied antecedent or the stone's masculine reference.
models.target: Reference changes from Britain/the island to the stone; pronoun gender and case are contextualized.
Translate the entire rescue through its final interpretation, using every printed support as needed.
models.model: Then, after a long time, when we raised our gaze from a distance, we saw on Farne, the island, the father Æthelwald, dear to God, coming out of his secluded place, so that he might watch our journey and see what was happening to us, for he heard the crashing of the storms and of the seething sea. When he then looked at us and saw us placed in distress and despair, he bent his knees to the Father of our Lord and Saviour Christ and prayed for our safety and our life. And when he completed that prayer, he then at the same time both calmed the swollen sea and stilled the storm, so that the violence of the storm ceased entirely and favourable winds brought us to land through the very calm sea. When we then came up onto land and also carried our ship up from the waves, the same storm soon returned and came again: it had ceased for a short time for our sake, and it was very great and strong all that day. Thus people could clearly understand that the short period of calm which had come there was granted from heaven at the prayers of that man of God for our rescue.
models.translation_origin: Curriculum designer independent translation witness, prepared before viewing source-editor or coordinator private witnesses.

models.model: They see Æthelwald; Æthelwald prays; the sea becomes calm; they reach land; the storm returns. Before it returns, they have come ashore and carried the ship up from the waves.
models.diagnosis: Do not end the episode at the calm or put the renewed storm before the landing.
models.target: Reconstruct chronology from temporal clauses and the complete resolution.

models.model: Ðæt hē wolde ūrne sīðfæt scēawian, and gesēon hwæt ūs gelumpe gives his purpose: to watch their journey and see what was happening to them. For-ðon hē gehīerde … gives his reason: he heard the crashing of the storm and sea. The purpose's wolde is locally explained as might/in order to, not merely a statement of past desire.
models.diagnosis: Do not confuse the dependent question hwæt … gelumpe inside the purpose with the outer purpose clause.
models.target: Purpose and factual cause in a complex actual sentence without treating volition as the only force of wolde.

models.model: Tō ðon ðætte introduces the outcome: all the storm's violence ceased, and favourable winds carried the sailors to land through the very calm sea. The actual wæs blinnende follows its supplied periphrastic analysis, not a newly invented progressive system.
models.diagnosis: This is the narrated result, not simply Æthelwald's desired outcome.
models.target: Result relation and coordinated outcomes; supported participial wording is not an unannounced tense system.

models.model: Mid-ðȳ hē ðā ūs ēac scēawode … describes Æthelwald seeing their distress; the main action begins ðā biegde hē his cnēowu. Mid-ðȳ wē ðā ūp cōmon tō lande … includes landing and carrying the ship up; the main action begins ðā sōna se ilca storm ęft hwearf and cōm.
models.diagnosis: The coordinated action inside the second temporal clause belongs before the renewed storm; do not stop the clause at lande.
models.target: Temporal clause boundaries and correlative main-clause continuation in the source.

models.model: Here wæs gebiddende means prayed (or was praying as an idiomatic English contextual rendering). Cook refers back to his note that this present-participle-plus-be construction can express a simple past, as it does here. It is therefore unsafe to infer a universal English progressive category from the shape.
models.diagnosis: The supplied source construction is not independently productive tense teaching.
models.target: Respect a source-local participial periphrasis and avoid an invented universal progressive equation.

models.model: People understand that the brief calm was granted from heaven, at the prayers of the man of God, for the sailors' rescue. Godes depends on weres; the man's prayers are named by bēnum, and ūre identifies the rescued sailors. Forgiefen means given/granted here, not forgiven.
models.diagnosis: Do not translate the rescue as a forgiveness or make God the person whose prayers are named.
models.target: Final content-clause interpretation and nested genitives; given is not automatically forgiven.

models.model: No. The storm returns once the people and ship are safely ashore and remains severe throughout that day. Its short suspension at the needed moment supports the narrator's interpretation that the calm was specially granted for their rescue in answer to prayer.
models.diagnosis: The conclusion requires the ending of the passage, not an isolated sentence about a calm sea.
models.target: Read the complete resolution and separate a temporary event from a permanent change.

models.prompt_original: Gold is more precious (64) than silver.
models.model: Gold is dēorwierðre ðonne seolfor.
audit_notes: Comparative predicate is weak neuter singular; no superlative is substituted.
models.target: Weak neuter singular comparative predicate; parallel nominative comparison standard; singular mass-metal nouns.

models.prompt_original: Righteousness is more precious than gold.
models.model: Rihtwīsnes is dēorwierðre ðonne gold.
audit_notes: Comparative predicate is weak feminine singular with rihtwīsnes.
models.target: Weak feminine singular comparative agrees with righteousness; the comparison standard has its own grammatical gender.

models.prompt_original: The bath is hot.
models.model: Ðæt bæð is hāt.
models.target: Singular neuter noun and agreeing positive predicate adjective.

models.prompt_original: The baths are hot.
models.model: Ðā baðu sindon hāt.
audit_notes: Long hāt has endingless strong neuter plural; baðu is neuter plural.
models.target: The lexical plural stem of bath; neuter plural predicate and plural copula.

models.prompt_original: The animals are living.
models.model: Ðā dēor sindon cwicu.
models.target: A living adjective predicate with the plural animal subject; English living need not force a new progressive tense.

models.prompt_original: Some pearls are black.
models.model: Suma męregrēotan sindon blaca.
models.target: Weak feminine pearl plural, an indefinite quantity and strong feminine plural black predicate.

models.prompt_original: The island is beautiful.
models.model: Ðæt īgland is fæger.
models.target: Neuter singular island and the selected beautiful adjective predicate.

models.prompt_original: Dolphins swim through the water.
models.model: Męreswīn swimmað þurh ðæt wæter.
audit_notes: Original indefinite dolphins has no required article; ðurh governs accusative.
models.target: Plural dolphins as swimming subjects; spatial through governs an accusative path.

models.prompt_original: Here are fishes often caught.
models.model: Hēr sindon fiscas oft fangen.
audit_notes: Selected fōn catch takes the ordinary patient in active and passive; bare past participle permitted by prior predicate-participle variation and newly supplied lexical pair.
models.target: Present agentless passive with a newly productive catch participle base, a plural subject, and here/often adverbs.

models.prompt_original: The night is more beautiful than the day.
models.model: Sēo niht is fægerre ðonne se dæg.
models.target: Weak feminine singular comparative beautiful; nominative day as the parallel comparison standard.

models.prompt_original: The city was distinguished with walls and gates.
models.model: Sēo ceaster wæs geweorðod mid weallum and gatum.
audit_notes: Original says was, not is. Walls and gates are dative after instrumental mid.
models.target: Past agentless distinguished/adorned predicate; city as subject, walls and gates as dative equipment after with.

models.prompt_original: Summer comes, and then winter.
models.model: Sumer cymð, and ðonne cymð winter.
audit_notes: Repeating cymð makes the original elliptical second predicate explicit without changing its meaning.
models.target: Selected summer/winter nouns, productive then adverb and recoverable repeated coming predicate.

models.prompt_original: The sun shines over all.
models.model: Sēo sunne scīnð ofer eall.
audit_notes: Eall is substantival neuter accusative singular everything, not an unmarked invented singular noun.
models.target: Singular astronomical sun, ordinary shining, and over plus a substantival all interpretation; identify the intended referent and case.

models.prompt_original: The old man came to the house.
models.model: Se ealda mann cōm tō ðǣm hūse.
models.target: Weak old adjective within a definite noun phrase, past coming and the previously taught destination frame.

models.prompt_original: Here are also found lead and iron.
models.model: Hēr sindon ēac lēad and īsern funden.
models.target: Two coordinated metal subjects with a plural present passive found predicate; preserve the here/also information.

models.prompt_original: Put not your hand into the fire.
models.model: Ne dō ðīne hand on ðæt fȳr.
audit_notes: Singular addressee chosen; on plus accusative gives the goal of placing. Full hand paradigm already supplies endingless accusative.
models.target: Negative placement command; possessive hand as accusative object and fire as the accusative goal after on.

models.prompt_original: The soldier takes the gem.
models.model: Se cęmpa nimð ðone gimm.
models.target: Ordinary taking with an accusative gem; distinguish subject from object in a simple transitive clause.

models.prompt_original: The rain injures the tower.
models.model: Se regn scęðeð ðǣm torre.
audit_notes: Tower is dative with scęððan; final selected third singular spelling must match grammar audit.
models.target: The selected weak hurt/injure system and its dative patient, despite the English direct-object wording.

models.prompt_original: The whale swims.
models.model: Se hwæl swimð.
models.target: A singular whale subject and the ordinary intransitive swimming frame.

models.prompt_original: Fishermen caught seals.
models.model: Fisceras fēngon sēolas.
models.target: Plural past catching with an accusative seal plural; apply the selected h-loss and vowel-length alternation.

models.prompt_original: The hungry sheep are not fed.
models.model: Ðā hungrigan scēap ne sindon fēded.
audit_notes: Weak hungrigan agrees with plural neuter scēap; this is a passive statement, not a negative command.
models.target: Definite hungry sheep with adjective agreement and a negative plural passive fed predicate; use the local negative-copula help as needed.

models.prompt_original: The man’s wife is beautiful.
models.model: Ðæs mannes wīf is fæger.
models.target: Possessor genitive and a beautiful predicate agreeing with the grammatical gender of wife.

models.prompt_original: Some men are black.
models.model: Sume męnn sindon blace.
models.target: Indefinite plural human subject and masculine plural black predicate; compare the feminine pearl target in16.6.

models.prompt_original: The carpenter will clothe his son.
models.model: Se trēowwyrhta scrȳt his sunu.
audit_notes: Present scrȳt has future reference licensed by the English task; no untaught infinitive of scrȳdan is silently promoted.
models.target: Clothing takes the accusative son; the personal genitive refers to the carpenter. Preserve future reference or a defensible volitional reading of will.

models.prompt_original: Depart from me, for I am (om. a) sinful man, (om. O) Lord.
models.model: Gewīt fram mē, for-ðon-ðe ic eom synfull mann, Dryhten.
audit_notes: Singular command route; original omission controls do not remove ordinary bare predicate mann. Dryhten is direct address.
models.target: Singular departure command with from plus dative, factual cause and direct address; preserve Cook’s article and O omission controls.

models.prompt_original: They shall drink, but ye shall be thirsty.
models.model: Hīe drincað, ac gē bēoð ðurstige.
audit_notes: Simple presents can bear the indicated future reference; adjective ðurstige agrees with the addressed plural, with ordinary copula.
models.target: Coordinate future-reference drinking and a thirsty adjective predicate; distinguish third-person and second-person plural subjects.

models.prompt_original: He said to her, Give me, I beseech thee, water to drink; for I am thirsty.
models.model: Hē sægde hiere: Sęle mē, ic bidde ðē, wæter drincan; for-ðon-ðe ic eom ðurstig.
audit_notes: Give-to-drink remains the explicitly supplied whole construction from Unit10, with plain drincan and no tō. Biddan selects accusative person ðē; parenthetic clause retained.
models.target: Dative female addressee in the speech frame, direct command, accusative person entreated, supplied give-to-drink expression, and factual cause with thirsty predicate.

models.prompt_original: He is not (om. a) God of (om. the) dead, but of (om. the) living.
models.model: Hē nis God dēadra, ac cwicra.
audit_notes: Bare strong generic genitive plurals dēadra/cwicra; no unintroduced libbende system.
models.target: Bare strong genitive plural personal adjectives for dead and living; adversative coordination and the supplied negative copula.

models.prompt_original: The sun shines on (ofer) the righteous and the unrighteous.
models.model: Sēo sunne scīnð ofer ðā rihtwīsan and ðā unrihtwīsan.
models.target: Over plus accusative personal-adjective groups, with their explicit definiteness and appropriate weak endings.

models.prompt_original: Ye are (om. the) light of the world.
models.model: Gē sindon ðǣre worulde lēoht.
audit_notes: Ðǣre worulde is the ordinary genitive the world; bare lēoht is the predicate.
models.target: Plural personal subject with the mass-noun predicate light and a world genitive; obey the original article-omission control.

models.prompt_original: The twelve gates were twelve pearls.
models.model: Ðā twęlf gatu wǣron twęlf męregrēotan.
models.target: The familiar twelve numeral with plural gates and pearls; a past identification clause with nominative predicates.

models.prompt_original: The street of the city was gold.
models.model: Ðǣre ceastre strǣt wæs gold.
models.target: Street as subject, city as its genitive possessor, and bare gold as a noun predicate.

models.prompt_original: Those that ate were four thousand men (154. c), besides women and children.
models.model: Ðā ðe ǣton wǣron fēower ðūsend manna, būtan wīfum and bearnum.
audit_notes: The full fēower ðūsend manna phrase is supplied, with explicit higher-numeral government; būtan governs the following datives.
models.target: A relative identifying those who ate; retain the locally supplied higher-numeral/genitive phrase and use dative exclusion after besides.

models.prompt_original: Blessed (p.p.) be God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort.
models.model: Geblētsod sīe God, ūres Dryhtnes Hǣlendes Crīstes Fæder, mildheortnessa Fæder and ealre frōfre God.
audit_notes: Independent blessing: sīe is optative present subjunctive. Proper title Hǣlendes and Crīstes stand in apposition to Dryhtnes. Ealre agrees with genitive feminine frōfre.
models.target: A blessing wish with the specified past participle, title/name apposition in matching case, and nested genitives including mercies and comfort.

models.prompt_original: The winds were favorable.
models.model: Ðā windas wǣron gesyndige.
models.target: Plural wind subjects and an agreeing favorable predicate adjective in the past.

models.prompt_original: He wishes to watch their journey.
models.model: Hē wille hiera sīðfæt scēawian.
audit_notes: The subject is he and the possessor their; wishes is volitional willan with plain infinitive scēawian.
models.target: Volitional wish plus the new plain watch infinitive, with accusative journey and a third-person plural possessor.

models.prompt_original: The wind and the sea obey him.
models.model: Se wind and se sǣ hīerað him.
audit_notes: Sea uses the actual prior masculine paradigm; the coordinated subject takes plural hīerað and obey governs dative him.
models.target: Coordinated subjects control a plural verb; the new obey sense governs a dative person.

models.prompt_original: Not at all in vain fought I with death, as he fought with beasts.
models.model: Nālæs hōlunga feaht ic wið dēað, swā hē feaht wið dēor.
audit_notes: Bounded nālæs hōlunga phrase conveys not at all in vain; selected wið+accusative opponents. Swā-swā is the assigned as comparison, not inasmuch as.
models.target: Strong past fight forms, an accusative opponent after with, the negative manner expression, and a factual comparative as-clause.

models.prompt_original: The time draws near [approaches, 164] (om. the) birth of Christ.
models.model: Sēo tīd genēalǣcð Crīstes gebyrde.
audit_notes: The time is nominative subject; gebyrde is dative complement of approach, and Crīstes is genitive dependent on birth.
models.target: Temporal approach with a dative event approached and a genitive proper name; obey the original article-omission control.

models.prompt_original: It is the day when (ðe) he was born (ācenned).
models.model: Hit is se dæg ðe hē wæs ācenned.
audit_notes: Exact source hint ācenned has plain e; supplied passive participle, without a full new ācennan system.
models.target: Temporal relative after day and the exact supplied born participle in a past passive; no full birth-verb system is inferred.

models.prompt_original: O, wast thou with me, dearest, then, while I rose up against my doom (dōm)?
models.model: Ēalā, wǣre ðū mid mē, lēofosta, ðā, ðā-hwīle-ðe ic rās ūp ongēan mīnne dōm?
audit_notes: Then, while, up and against are all retained. Wǣre is second singular preterite indicative in the direct past question, not automatically subjunctive. Weak personal direct address lēofosta needs its bounded address frame.
models.target: A factual past question, accompaniment, weak personal adjective in direct address, temporal correlation/while, and rise-up opposition to fate.

models.prompt_original: The moon is hid (hȳdan, 113), the night is still.
models.model: Se mōna is hȳded, sēo niht is stillu.
audit_notes: Positive stillu is strong feminine nominative singular; e-class dictionary final e does not eliminate the -u ending.
models.target: Singular astronomical moon with an agentless hidden predicate; coordinate the night’s positive still predicate without imposing participial syntax on it.

models.prompt_original: Thou bringst the fisher to his wife.
models.model: Ðū bringst ðone fiscere tō his wīfe.
audit_notes: Bringan takes accusative traveller and tō+dative destination/person.
models.target: Second singular bringing with an accusative person and a dative destination/person; the possessor belongs to the fisherman.

models.prompt_original: Calm is the morn(ing).
models.model: Smylte is se morgen.
models.target: A nominative calm predicate and the morning subject; preserve the sense despite predicate-first English order.

models.prompt_original: I know that this was life.
models.model: Ic wāt ðæt ðis wæs līf.
audit_notes: Life is līf; original does not say wife or wile.
models.target: Known finite content-clause syntax, demonstrative reference, and past identification with the noun life.

models.prompt_original: What do ye more than they?
models.model: Hwæt dōð gē mā ðonne hīe?
audit_notes: Mā is amount adverb; comparative standard hīe is nominative with do understood. Hwæt is object of dōð.
models.target: A direct object question with second plural do; adverbial more compares the amount of doing and admits an understood repeated predicate.
